GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: A MachineMonster port and one of the two seam pins in this batch, so the comparison is node by node against Fogmog.cs:38-58 and against `py audit/tools/state_machine_probes.py mismatch`, whose 12 resolved pairs list Fogmog among the 7 EXACT matches (it is not one of G1's five misreaders). Nodes: ILLUSION_MOVE (initial) -> SWIPE_MOVE -> BRANCH; SWIPE_RANDOM_MOVE -> HEADBUTT_MOVE -> SWIPE_MOVE. BRANCH is added SWIPE_RANDOM first then HEADBUTT (Fogmog.cs:46-47), both overload #6 (`MoveRepeatType, Func<float>`) so there is no integer to misread at all: CannotRepeat, weights 0.4f and 0.6f. fogmog.py:82-83 adds them in the same order with the same weights and repeat type. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py machine`, seeds b01-b03, 40 turns): identical sequences and identical MonsterAi draw counts (17/17, 18/18, 16/16) -- the draw count is below 40 precisely because SWIPE_RANDOM -> HEADBUTT -> SWIPE is a deterministic leg.

guards.what: Add order is observable and this branch has UNEQUAL weights, so a swap would show as a 40/60 flip
guards.rationale: monster_state_machine step 14: one NextFloat(total) then subtract-and-walk in add order. Recorded explicitly because the sibling unit inklet in this same batch has the reversed-order defect and the two must not be assumed to share a fate (PROMPT.md bug class 29 -- never copy a sibling's verdict). Here the executed sequence diff pins both the order and the weights.

guards.what: SWIPE_MOVE and SWIPE_RANDOM_MOVE are two distinct ids sharing ONE delegate (Fogmog.cs:42-43, both `SwipeMove`); the port keeps them distinct (fogmog.py:75-76, both `self._swipe_move`)
guards.rationale: Load-bearing, because the two nodes have different follow-ups (SWIPE -> BRANCH, SWIPE_RANDOM -> HEADBUTT) and different CannotRepeat identities inside BRANCH. Collapsing them would change the graph. monster_state_machine G8's dormancy note calls this pair 'the game's own near-miss' for duplicate state ids; the port keeps the ids distinct too, so no duplicate-key question arises.

guards.what: IllusionMove is guarded by `base.CombatState.IsLiveCombat()` (Fogmog.cs:64) and the port summons unconditionally (fogmog.py:93-95)
guards.rationale: Executed: CombatState.cs:608 `public bool IsLiveCombat() { return true; }` -- the real combat state's implementation is a constant true, and the only other implementers are ICombatState.cs's declaration and NullCombatState.cs (a mock). So the guard is a test/mock hatch, never false in a shipping combat, and the port's unconditional summon is the shipping behaviour. This is PROMPT.md bug class 18's shape checked before verdicting.

guards.what: The summoned Eye With Teeth is added during the ENEMY side, where CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded declines to roll a move (monster_state_machine step 48 / G9 clause b)
guards.rationale: G9 clause b is the seam's dormant gap and is not re-verdicted. It cannot bite through THIS summon anyway, because EyeWithTeeth is a hand-rolled Monster with no machine and no roll on either side: executed, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain` shows 0 MonsterAi draws over 20 of its turns. The sim's CreatureCmd.add does roll the spawn's parity HP on the Niche stream before it joins the list (cmds.py:249-253), mirroring CreateCreature, and assigns the CombatId in attach order.
